title: Home water controller — fictional founder disclosure
input_summary: Fictional example: I want a home water controller that watches how long water flows without stopping. When I mark the home as away and water keeps flowing beyond a set time, it notifies me and closes a motorized main-water valve. I want to limit water damage while nobody is home. I have not built it, chosen the timer rule, or decided what happens if a sensor or the power fails.

executive_summary.text: The proposed device watches continuous water flow while a home is marked as away. After a selected duration, it would notify the homeowner and close the main-water valve. The intended benefit is limiting damage when nobody is present; no prototype or results were supplied.

The AI sees a possible core combination: an away-state condition, a continuous-flow duration rule, and a valve response. The founder should confirm whether their interaction is the intended technical focus.
executive_summary.inference_reason: These three disclosed steps determine when the system acts; the actual detection and failure-handling logic remains unknown.

executive_summary.text: Public examples show that water monitoring and automatic shutoff already appear in commercial product descriptions. The practical next step is to specify the actual decision rule and handling of normal use, false alarms, and failures. This is a development question, not a conclusion about patentability.

evidence.locator: Automatic Water Shut Off; Internal Leak Sensor

problem.text: A homeowner may not be present to respond when water continues flowing unexpectedly.
It is unknown how often this problem occurs in the intended homes or which existing workaround the founder currently uses.

solution.text: Measure continuous flow duration, check whether the home is marked away, notify the homeowner, and close a motorized main-water valve when the duration exceeds a selected setting.
Sensor choice, timer reset behavior, notification timing, and power-failure behavior are not yet specified.

advantages.text: Intended advantage: limit water damage while nobody is home. No measured reduction has been demonstrated.
advantages.evidence_needed: Compare detected events, water released before closure, false shutoffs, and response time against a defined baseline.

advantages.text: An away-state condition might allow a different response policy than when the home is occupied.
advantages.inference_reason: The description gates action on a user-selected away state, but supplies no comparison showing a benefit.
advantages.evidence_needed: Explain and test what changes between home and away states; measure missed events and nuisance shutoffs.

questions.question: Exactly what starts, pauses, and resets the continuous-flow timer?
questions.why_it_matters: This defines the decision mechanism and distinguishes continuous flow from intermittent normal use.
questions.suggested_evidence: A state diagram and three example timelines, including a brief interruption.

questions.question: What changes when the home is marked away, and how is that state selected?
questions.why_it_matters: The interaction between user state and the shutoff rule may be central to the proposed mechanism.
questions.suggested_evidence: Home/away behavior comparison and rule pseudocode.

questions.question: What should happen during a false alarm, sensor failure, or loss of power?
questions.why_it_matters: The described response does not yet explain reliability or recovery.
questions.suggested_evidence: Failure scenarios and a prototype test plan; mark proposed behavior separately from tested behavior.
